name: Barabbas
summary: At the feast the governor released one prisoner to the people, and there was a notable prisoner named Barabbas, who lay bound with those who had made insurrection with him and had committed murder in the insurrection (Matthew 27:15-16; Mark 15:6-7). Luke states the charge plainly: he had been cast into prison for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder (Luke 23:18-19). The chief priests moved the people to ask for Barabbas, and Pilate released him and delivered Jesus to their will (Mark 15:11; Luke 23:25).
offenseFull: Barabbas was not an unknown man. He was a notable prisoner, taken with a band that had risen against the government and killed in the rising (Mark 15:6-7; Luke 23:18-19). John calls him a robber (John 18:40). He was not brought out because his cause had been heard and he was found innocent; he was brought out because the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude to ask for him and to destroy Jesus (Matthew 27:20).

Peter afterward set the exchange before the people in plain words: they denied the Holy One and the Just, desired a murderer to be granted to them, and killed the Prince of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which the apostles were witnesses (Acts 3:14-15). That is the offense of this case as the apostles preached it. Peter said in the same breath that through ignorance they did it, as did also their rulers, and then called them to repent and be converted so that their sins might be blotted out (Acts 3:17-19). The crowd that shouted for a murderer was not written off. It was preached to.
judgmentFull: Pilate said a third time that he found no cause of death in him, and asked what evil the man had done (Luke 23:22). He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Matthew records how the choice was put, whether he should release Barabbas or Jesus which is called Christ, and gives the governor’s own reading of the court: he knew that for envy they had delivered him (Matthew 27:17-18). His own wife sent word to him while he sat on the judgment seat, telling him to have nothing to do with that just man (Matthew 27:19). The envy was written on their faces and in their spirit and they could not hide it, and a heathen governor could see it from the bench.

So the guilty man went free and the innocent man was delivered to their will (Mark 15:15; Luke 23:25). No further history of Barabbas is given, and no penalty on him is recorded anywhere in the gospels. He stands in the book as a man spared, and spared in the very proceeding that laid the sentence he had earned on another. The rule the court broke is written: he that justifies the wicked, and he that condemns the just, are both an abomination to the Lord (Proverbs 17:15). And the release is not the end of the reckoning, because the same word that named the exchange also named the day when he whom they pierced will be looked on and mourned for (Zechariah 12:10).

lawsResolved.text: Those guilty of murder are to be put to death.
Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
The judge that justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination to God.

text.text: Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.
And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
Now at that feast he released unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they desired.
And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas:
(Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)
But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.
And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
But ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you;
And killed the Prince of life, whom God hath raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses.
And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers.
But those things, which God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.
Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.
Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?
For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.
When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.
He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.

And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.
And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?
For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.
When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.
But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
